about: The two books the agents work from. The engineering book is the authority on the frameworks and their definitions (the number line, aggregate efficiency, honest data, regeneration, the governor, the end game); the operating manual is the authority on business models and how to run them. Where they define the same thing differently, the engineering book wins, because it is the newer and deeper of the two. Every price, cost, volume and timeline in either book is an example that shows an idea, never a fact about FreeWater: decisions use numbers from the platform's own books or from real quotes.
rules: Take the ideas and the reasoning from the books. Take every number from the platform's own books (the ledger) or a real quote.
Cite the passages a decision relied on, by their ids.
Where the two books differ on a framework or definition, the engineering book wins; on how to run a business model, the operating manual leads.
Mark every claim as one of two kinds, as the books do: a buildable plan (costed, checkable now) or a stress test (an idea run past its limits to find where the real constraints sit).
